$comment: Browser registry for the memory benchmark. Adding a browser is a JSON edit,
not a code change, as long as it belongs to one of the launch families in
bundlePath and executableName accept a string or an array of candidates;
the first combination that exists on disk wins. Vendors rename their
bundles between releases (Zen shipped as both 'Zen Browser.app' and
'Zen.app'), so candidates are cheaper than a support ticket.
extraBlankTabs records tabs a browser opens on its own beyond the workload
URLs, so the report can disclose the real tab count instead of comparing

browsers.label: Blanc
notes: main.js creates one blanc://newtab at startup in addition to the URLs
passed on the command line — hence extraBlankTabs: 1.
Do NOT set BLANC_TEST=1 for a benchmark run: acceptanceTestMode in
main.js disables ad blocking, which would measure a configuration the

browsers.label: Blanc (blocking off)
notes: Isolates what the built-in blocker contributes. The runner seeds
settings.json in the throwaway profile with adblockEnabled: false.

browsers.label: Firefox
notes: Worth running alongside Zen: it separates what Zen's own changes cost
from what Gecko costs, which is the honest way to read a Zen result.

browsers.label: Arc
notes: Arc manages its own profile/space model and may ignore --user-data-dir.
Verify with --keep-profiles that the throwaway profile was actually
populated before trusting an Arc row.

browsers.label: Safari
unsupportedReason: Safari has no command-line profile isolation and no command-line tab
opening, so it cannot be measured on the same terms as the others: a
run would use the tester's real profile, with their extensions, their
history and their iCloud tabs. Driving it over AppleScript is possible
but the profile problem remains, so a Safari row would not be
comparable and is deliberately omitted rather than footnoted.

browsers.label: Orion
unsupportedReason: WebKit-based with no documented command-line profile or tab interface.
